title: grafana-plugin-compat: paired .test.ts / .compat.test.ts per function, shared srv mocks in utils/mocks.ts
answers: Where are plugin-compat datasource functions implemented and tested?
How do I add a new @grafana/plugin-compat wrapper function with both new-API and legacy-fallback coverage?
Where is the mock DataSourceSrv/BackendSrv used in plugin-compat tests defined?
body:
Each wrapped function lives in its own file under packages/grafana-plugin-compat/src/<domain>/<fnName>.ts and is re-exported from a barrel file like packages/grafana-plugin-compat/src/datasources.ts. Two test files accompany each: `<fnName>.test.ts` mocks `@grafana/runtime/unstable` with the real function present (new-API path), and `<fnName>.compat.test.ts` mocks it as `undefined` to exercise the legacy `getDataSourceSrv()`/`getBackendSrv()` fallback path. Shared mock factories (getMockedDatasourceSrv, getMockedBackendSrv) live in packages/grafana-plugin-compat/src/utils/mocks.ts and must stay excluded from tsconfig.build.json's compiled output since it's test-only.
Use this layout when adding any new plugin-compat wrapper function.

Shared mock factories (getMockedDatasourceSrv, getMockedBackendSrv) are defined in packages/grafana-plugin-compat/src/utils/mocks.ts and must be excluded from tsconfig.build.json's compiled output since they are test-only. Functions are re-exported via barrel files like packages/grafana-plugin-compat/src/datasources.ts. Follow this structure when adding new plugin-compat wrappers to ensure both modern and legacy API paths are tested.
